stem: Why should heavy plant debris and media be removed before applying many disinfectants?
choices: Heavy debris mainly matters because it can trap moisture and change local room conditions.
Debris should be removed mainly so labels and surface markings remain visible during disinfection.
Organic material can shield microorganisms and interfere with disinfectant contact or effectiveness, so cleaning should come first.
Cleaning first is needed only for metal tools because porous greenhouse surfaces are disinfected differently.
rationale: Disinfectants work best when they can contact the surface or organism they are intended to act on. Plant debris, media, soil, and other organic material can physically shield microorganisms or reduce the effectiveness of some disinfectants. Removing heavy contamination before disinfection is therefore part of a controlled sanitation sequence, not just a cosmetic step.
